definition: serving as a symbol of something
memoryTip: Like an emblem — stands for a bigger idea or era.
correctPassage: The abandoned mill became emblematic of the town’s industrial decline.
wrongPassages: Investors wanted emblematic markets where prices never moved more than a cent.
The blank page was called emblematic of a report packed with charts and findings.
Her thoroughly ordinary lunch order was somehow emblematic of radical innovation.

memoryTip: A-bate: turn down the volume — reduction (noise abatement).
correctPassage: Noise abatement measures cut late-night complaints from nearby residents.
wrongPassages: Noise abatement measures made the street twice as loud overnight.
They packed a spare abatement next to the tire.
City hall issued an abatement license for favorite colors only.

definition: lack of harmony; clash of sounds or ideas
memoryTip: Dis-sonance: harsh sound or clash — ideas that don’t fit.
correctPassage: Voters sensed dissonance between the campaign’s promises and its budget plan.
wrongPassages: The choir’s perfect unison was praised as pure dissonance from first note to last.
There was total dissonance among the panel: every member repeated the same conclusion.
She stored the dissonance in a drawer beside rubber bands and spare badges.

definition: reduce in extent or cut short
memoryTip: Cut the tail short — reduce or trim back.
correctPassage: Budget cuts will curtail after-school programs for the rest of the year.
wrongPassages: Budget cuts will curtail spending by doubling every department’s budget.
Please curtail the window before you leave.
She stored the curtail on a shelf with packing tape.

definition: courage and strength in pain or adversity
memoryTip: Fort + attitude — inner strength when things get hard.
correctPassage: Survivors showed remarkable fortitude during the long months of recovery.
wrongPassages: His fortitude collapsed into pure bravery that never wavered under fire.
They packed a spare fortitude in the trunk.
The paint color “Fortitude Mist” is a standard beige.
